john-kiriakou.body_append:
## The night of arrest and the garage

On Covert Strategies Revealed in July 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said that on the night of his 2012 arrest — after the FBI released him and he was back at home — he told his wife he was going to stay up to watch television. He was not. He was going, he said, to the garage: *"start the car and lay on the back seat and just let it finish me."* His wife suspected. She insisted he come upstairs to bed. *"I said, 'No, I'm not ready.' She said, 'I'm insisting.'"*<Cite t="08:12" /><Cite t="08:42" /> The next day his brother told him *"this is going to turn out to be the best thing that ever happened to you"*; his ex-wife told him he had to keep talking about the case because *"eventually they're going to move on to their next target — and your side of the story will become the side of record."* They did, and it did — the next target, he said, was [Edward Snowden](/wiki/edward-snowden).<Cite t="08:42" /><Cite t="09:12" /><Cite t="09:42" />

## June 30, 2018 — 'worse than prison'

Kiriakou identifies 30 June 2018 — three years and change out of federal prison, the day his divorce was finalised — as *"the worst day of my life. Okay? Because well in Latin the words 'in flagrante delicto' mean something."* He describes suffering from severe insomnia, lying in bed at three in the morning and asking his Alexa device *"what percentage of marriages that begin as affairs end in divorce?"* — to which the answer came back *"93 percent"* — and then turning to his bedroom iconostasis and quietly asking, aloud, of the family icons of St Nectarios: *"Am I really that bad of a guy that I deserve this?"* He was tempted, he said, to *"start boycotting church, which I had never done before,"* and rejected the temptation with the thought *"that's what the devil wants me to do."*<Cite t="10:16" /><Cite t="10:46" /><Cite t="11:18" /><Cite t="11:49" /><Cite t="12:21" />

## The Bedford basement and the Juárez shelter

Asked in July 2026 how his own arc had settled, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said he had told his younger sister, Tina — five years younger and, he said, *"my best friend, really"* — that the only thing he still feared was dying alone after a long illness. His sister told him to stop being ridiculous: he would live in the enormous house she and her family have in Bedford, New Hampshire, in *"this beautiful apartment"* she had prepared in the basement.<Cite t="1:20:16" /><Cite t="1:20:48" /> The host, whose organisation runs a shelter for unaccompanied migrant women with children in Juárez, Mexico, offered an alternative: the shelter's director had said Kiriakou would be welcome in his old age at the Juárez shelter if he needed somewhere else to go.<Cite t="1:21:21" />

## Living with two elderly gay men on oxygen

Recalling how strained his finances were in the years after prison, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said he became so *"broke and unemployable"* that he had to rent a room in a house with two elderly gay men who were attached to oxygen machines *"walking around like smoking cigarettes with their oxygen"* — an arrangement whose evenings were *"Jeopardy at seven, Wheel of Fortune at seven-thirty. I'm sitting there like this — like, well, I guess this is the way it's going to be."*<Cite t="1:19:45" /><Cite t="1:20:16" />

## The Diary of a CEO shorts and the Gen Z breakout

The January 2026 [Diary of a CEO](/wiki/diary-of-a-ceo-january-2026) interview, cut into TikTok shorts by a University of Texas at Austin sophomore, is the moment [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) identifies as the pivot after which his short-form audience exploded; the Creative Artists Agency signed him by telephone at 2:30 in the morning while he was on a paid contract in Dubai.<Cite t="19:41" /><Cite t="20:13" /><Cite t="20:44" /> By mid-2026 he was running the [cameo practice](/wiki/kiriakou-cameo-practice) at 25 to 30 hours a week — 900 messages in the month of March alone, nearly 2,000 total by July — of which three recipients later credited him with talking them out of suicide.<Cite t="1:07:18" /><Cite t="1:07:50" /><Cite t="1:08:22" /><Cite t="1:08:52" />

mk-ultra.body_append:
## MK Chickwit, San Francisco and the French village bakery

On Covert Strategies Revealed in July 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) detailed several sub-operations of [MK Ultra](/wiki/mk-ultra) he says are documented but under-known. Under MK Chickwit, the [CIA](/wiki/cia) broke into a laboratory in Switzerland to steal the formula for LSD *"so we could make it better."* The agency then chose San Francisco as *"the sort of the headquarters of these experiments,"* recruiting a contingent of sex workers who picked up men on the street, dosed them with LSD and brought them to an agency safe house to *"tie them down and get them to confess their deepest, darkest secrets"* — an experiment Kiriakou says produced only *"jabbering incoherently"* and *"freakouts."*<Cite t="38:31" /><Cite t="39:04" /><Cite t="39:35" /> A further protocol involved a small French village whose entire bread supply came from one bakery: agents broke into the bakery at night and dosed the yeast, so that everyone in the village who bought the next morning's bread went on an LSD trip together. *"For decades we were like, 'It wasn't us, it wasn't us, it wasn't us.' And then in the '90s we're like, 'Okay, it was us.'"*<Cite t="40:07" /><Cite t="40:38" /><Cite t="41:09" />

## The Church Committee, the $500 fine and the hat in the corridor

After Senators Frank Church and Otis Pike subpoenaed the [family jewels](/wiki/mk-ultra) in 1975, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says the CIA director was expressly ordered by Church not to destroy the MK Ultra documents. The director, he says, *"literally went from Capitol Hill back to headquarters and said, 'Destroy everything.'"* Eighty-five percent of the MK Ultra archive was shredded — *"that's why we have this little idea after all these years of what it was"* — and the director was held in contempt of Congress and fined $500. On Kiriakou's account, the old-timers who trained him told him that every CIA employee lined the corridors when the director walked back into headquarters after being fined, throwing dollars and $5 bills into a hat to pay his $500 penalty *"just as a big FU to Congress."*<Cite t="42:12" /><Cite t="42:44" /><Cite t="43:17" /><Cite t="43:49" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) locates [Project Gateway](/wiki/project-gateway) — the CIA's Cold War astral-projection line of work — inside the broader [MK Ultra](/wiki/mk-ultra) programme (1952–1975), which he says the agency accelerated only after being told, incorrectly, that the Soviets were experimenting with ESP and mind-reading?
project-gateway.body_append:
## Origin as a sub-programme of MK Ultra

On Covert Strategies Revealed in July 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said [Project Gateway](/wiki/project-gateway) is best understood as one strand of the wider [MK Ultra](/wiki/mk-ultra) programme, which ran from 1952 to 1975 and included *"ESP, astral projection, mind reading, LSD and using LSD to get people to confess to their deepest, darkest secrets."* Kiriakou says the entire enterprise began after the [CIA](/wiki/cia) recruited *"a fake, a phony source who said 'the Russians are experimenting with this'"* — a claim Kiriakou says was untrue, though the Chinese were. *"We're behind the eight-ball,"* the agency told itself, and poured resources into the ESP-and-LSD portfolio on a false premise.<Cite t="36:58" /><Cite t="37:28" /><Cite t="38:00" />

executive-order-12333.body_append:
## Church-era assassination ban and the 12 September 2001 revision

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said on Covert Strategies Revealed in July 2026 that the original 1975 signed version of [Executive Order 12333](/wiki/executive-order-12333) — imposed at the insistence of Senator Frank Church and Congressman Otis Pike after the [Church Committee](/wiki/church-committee) — expressly *"forbade assassinations"* by the [CIA](/wiki/cia). That prohibition survived, in his telling, *"until September 12th, 2001,"* the day after the attacks, when President George W. Bush *"kind of crossed that part out"* and effectively authorised the agency to *"kill anybody you want. And that's what they've been doing ever since."*<Cite t="43:49" /><Cite t="44:20" /><Cite t="44:51" />

dyk_append: … that the man [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) knew inside the counter-terrorism centre as the friendly *"nice guy"* who ran the [Tuesday-morning kill list](/wiki/tuesday-morning-kill-list) — the head of the CIA's Special Activities Division — was revealed in a 2007 Vanity Fair article to have been, before joining the agency, a hitman for the Cali cocaine cartel?
tuesday-morning-kill-list.body_append:
## The Special Activities Division chief who had been a Cali cartel hitman

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) has described the man he identifies only as *"Rick"* — the head of the CIA's Special Activities Division — as *"the friendliest guy in the world,"* the colleague who greeted the counter-terrorism centre every morning with *"morning, fellas."* When Kiriakou asked another colleague what Rick actually did, the answer was that on Tuesday mornings Rick collected the [kill list](/wiki/tuesday-morning-kill-list) drawn up in the White House Counsel's office, sent his men to the named targets around the world, and returned the following Tuesday for the next list.<Cite t="29:34" /><Cite t="30:06" /><Cite t="30:39" />

In 2007 — three years after Kiriakou left the [CIA](/wiki/cia) — Vanity Fair published an exposé of the same man. Rick, Kiriakou says, had earlier been a hitman for the Cali cocaine cartel, and had been recruited into the agency by a *"dark figure"* who later became the deputy director for operations because both men were working against communist insurgents in Colombia. *"The Cali cartel hated the communists and vice versa. Well, the CIA hated the communists — and the enemy of my enemy is my friend."* The eventual DDO's pitch to him, as Kiriakou paraphrases it: *"If you don't want to do cartel hits any more, I'm the CIA station chief down here. Why don't you come and do hits for me?"*<Cite t="31:10" /><Cite t="31:44" /><Cite t="32:15" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) recounts [Daniel Hale](/wiki/daniel-hale)'s account of a drone strike in which Hale had *"eyes on the target"* from Nevada and reported two young girls beside the man, only for his commander at McDill AFB to reply that they were goats — and, threatened with court martial, Hale fired the missile and killed a twelve-year-old and a nine-year-old girl?
daniel-hale.body_append:
## The 'those aren't kids, those are goats' strike

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) has recounted a specific mission that [Daniel Hale](/wiki/daniel-hale) — the U.S. Air Force drone operator turned whistleblower — described to him personally. Hale was operating the drone from a base in Nevada; his commander was at McDill Air Force Base in Florida; both had the same feed on screen. Hale reported *"I have eyes on the target,"* and the commander answered *"fire."* Hale said *"wait a minute, he's with two little kids."* The commander answered: *"Those aren't kids. Those are goats."* Hale insisted: *"I'm looking at them, they're not goats, they're children. They're girls."* The commander answered *"fire"* again. Hale refused. The commander threatened him with court martial. Hale fired the missile. He killed *"a 12-year-old girl and a nine-year-old girl."* Hale, in Kiriakou's telling, went home that night and told his girlfriend *"I became a child killer today."*<Cite t="32:46" /><Cite t="33:18" /><Cite t="33:49" />

Kennedy Jr.](/wiki/robert-f-kennedy-jr) told [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) that on 22 November 1963, minutes after his uncle's assassination, he watched his father say to CIA Director [John McCone](/wiki/john-mccone) in the Hickory Hill driveway *"tell me your people didn't do this"* — and that McCone answered *"I don't know who did it,"* not *"of course not"*?
john-mccone.body_append:
## The Hickory Hill driveway (November 1963)

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) has said [Robert F. Kennedy Jr.](/wiki/robert-f-kennedy-jr) told him personally about an exchange in the driveway of the Kennedy family's McLean, Virginia estate on 22 November 1963 — the day President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas. Kennedy Jr., then a schoolboy, had been pulled out of his junior high in McLean and driven home to Hickory Hill; his father, Robert F. Kennedy Sr., was standing in the driveway speaking with CIA Director [John McCone](/wiki/john-mccone). Kiriakou lays out the context: both families were devout Catholics; McCone's wife had died six months earlier of breast cancer; the Kennedys were sufficiently worried about McCone's mental state that he had been dining with them several nights a week, and he and Robert Kennedy would go swimming together after dinner. Kennedy Jr. said he walked past his father and heard him say to McCone: *"Tell me your people didn't do this."* On Kiriakou's telling of Kennedy Jr.'s account, McCone answered *"I don't know who did it"* — not, Kiriakou emphasises, *"of course not."*<Cite t="27:31" /><Cite t="28:02" /><Cite t="28:33" /><Cite t="29:03" />

pete-seeger.body_append:
## The uncalled Phil Ochs phone call

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou), for whom [Pete Seeger](/wiki/pete-seeger) was — along with his father and grandfather — one of the three formative figures of his early life, recounted on Covert Strategies Revealed in July 2026 a story Seeger told him personally. Seeger had been performing at a folk club in Greenwich Village. The set ran late, and he was packing up as quickly as he could to make the last train to Beacon, where he lived. A waitress told him *"[Phil Ochs](/wiki/phil-ochs) is on the phone for you."* Seeger asked her to tell Phil he would call him back the next day, and left for the train. Ochs — whose voice had been damaged by an African mugging that left him unable to reach high notes, and who had descended into deep depression as a result — committed suicide that same night. Kiriakou records what Seeger said to him: *"That selfish bastard. I'll never forgive him for what he did. He had no idea how many people he's hurt."* Kiriakou says he thought of it every time in his own dark years the temptation returned.<Cite t="1:15:36" /><Cite t="1:16:08" /><Cite t="1:16:38" />

dyk_append: … that on the night [Phil Ochs](/wiki/phil-ochs) killed himself, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says [Pete Seeger](/wiki/pete-seeger) had declined a phone call from him at a Greenwich Village folk club to catch the last train to Beacon — and afterwards told Kiriakou, uncharacteristically, *"that selfish bastard, I'll never forgive him for what he did"*?
phil-ochs.body_append:
## The unreturned Seeger phone call

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) has said on-record — attributing the account directly to [Pete Seeger](/wiki/pete-seeger) — that Ochs telephoned Seeger from a Greenwich Village folk club on the night of his death; Seeger, hurrying to catch the last train to Beacon, asked the waitress to tell Ochs he would call back tomorrow and left. Ochs, whose voice had been permanently damaged by an African mugging that left him unable to hit high notes and who had fallen into deep depression, killed himself that night. Seeger's uncharacteristic verdict, delivered to Kiriakou years afterwards, is what stuck in Kiriakou's memory: *"That selfish bastard. I'll never forgive him for what he did. He had no idea how many people he's hurt."*<Cite t="1:15:36" /><Cite t="1:16:08" /><Cite t="1:16:38" />
